script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Friday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed up zero point four two percent on the session. A mixed day across the nine primary holdings, with optics leading and memory dragging hard.

Applied Optoelectronics surged four point six seven percent on Friday, pulling the broader optics complex with it. AI data center demand is now pushing valuations into triple-digit territory — and the gap between growth excitement and financial reality may be wider than investors realize.

The Standard and Poor's five hundred posted a weekly gain of one point one percent, supported by strong hyperscaler earnings from Microsoft and Amazon. Soaring yields and oil prices weighed on the tape through midweek, but megacap tech delivered enough to sustain the broader risk-on tone heading into the weekend. No Federal Reserve speakers or major economic prints drove Friday's session directly.

The top story Friday belongs to Applied Optoelectronics. Shares surged four point six seven percent as a risk-on wave swept through the optics sector, with finance dot yahoo dot com reporting that optics stocks are outrunning the broader semiconductor rally on AI data center demand. The report specifically cited Applied Optoelectronics and Coherent as each gaining roughly seven percent, while Lumentum added approximately five percent. The framing from analysts is important here: valuations have moved into triple-digit territory, and commentary is explicitly flagging the gap between growth excitement and financial fundamentals. For this portfolio, which holds Applied Optoelectronics as its largest single position at seven point four three percent of assets, and Lumentum as a separate position at five point five zero percent, Friday's move was meaningful — but the analyst language around valuation discipline is worth monitoring closely as earnings season continues to sharpen expectations.

Applied Optoelectronics was up four point six seven percent on the session. As covered in the top story, AI data center demand is the primary catalyst, and optics names broadly outperformed semiconductors. The next test is whether earnings results can close the gap between current multiples and underlying financials. Redwire Corporation was up one point seven seven percent on the session. A comparison piece out Friday framed Redwire against Raytheon Technologies, highlighting Redwire's faster projected sales and earnings growth against Raytheon's record backlog and execution track record. Watch for any contract announcements or government budget developments that could sharpen that growth case.

Turning to AST SpaceMobile, which was up zero point nine two percent on the session. Multiple pieces circulated Friday, with the most forward-looking noting that BlueBird satellites eleven, twelve, and thirteen are set to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Nine from Cape Canaveral on August fifth, twenty twenty-six. Production is now advancing through satellite forty-two. Retail sentiment is shifting toward execution as the central narrative. The cash burn — reported at one point one billion dollars annually — remains the key risk. The August fifth launch is the immediate catalyst to watch.

Over at Nebius Group, shares were up one point zero five percent on the session. Separately, a headline flagged the collapse of Leopold Aschenbrenner's artificial intelligence hedge fund, which reportedly peaked at forty-five billion dollars before margin calls forced leveraged AI infrastructure positions to be sold to Citadel at a discount. Nebius, as an AI infrastructure name, operates in that same thematic space — forced institutional selling in leveraged AI vehicles is a macro risk worth tracking for the sector broadly.

Bloom Energy was down zero point six three percent on the session. A comparison piece out Friday noted that Bloom Energy has turned cash-flow positive while having deployed six hundred sixty-one million dollars in capital — a meaningful distinction from peers facing liquidity stress. A separate piece weighed Bloom against NextEra Energy, noting Bloom trades at a premium valuation. The cash-flow positive milestone is the key fundamental development to monitor.

Meanwhile, TeraWulf was down zero point nine zero percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move. The digital asset mining sector remained sensitive to broader risk sentiment and energy cost dynamics. Watch bitcoin price action and power cost headlines as the near-term read-through for this position.

Lumentum Holdings was up two point nine nine percent on the session. As noted in the Applied Optoelectronics coverage, the optics sector broadly caught a bid on AI data center demand. Lumentum's move was in line with that sector tailwind. Upcoming earnings commentary from hyperscalers on optical interconnect spending will be the next key input.

IREN Limited was down three point eight two percent on the session. No company-specific news accompanied the decline. The digital infrastructure and bitcoin mining names broadly underperformed Friday, and IREN moved with that sector pressure. Power contract and hash rate capacity updates remain the key near-term catalysts.

Sandisk Corporation was down five point zero nine percent on the session. Finance dot yahoo dot com reported that Sandisk is down forty-five percent over the past month, with the piece raising direct questions about whether memory investors should rotate to Micron or SK Hynix. Earnings are in the near-term queue, and that report will be the defining test for this position.

Three items to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Sandisk Corporation earnings — the exact date is imminent, and the report will address the forty-five percent one-month decline directly. Second, the AST SpaceMobile BlueBird satellite launch scheduled for August fifth aboard a SpaceX Falcon Nine — execution risk is live. Third, AMD earnings, flagged Friday alongside Sandisk — AMD results will set the tone for the broader semiconductor and AI infrastructure complex.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the AST SpaceMobile launch window and Sandisk earnings — both have the potential to move this portfolio meaningfully in either direction.
